clue.text: Consumer surveys could harm racketeers

indicators.note: could here suggests the letters of the next words might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A complaint that customer questionnaires could be harmful to gangsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could' signals the anagram of HARM RACKETEERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Market research means studies that gather shoppers' opinions and buying habits.

clue.text: Better prepared to pass on into the back

indicators.note: into tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the back or rear
to pass on is a euphemism for to die

explanation.surface: Someone more ready to move a ball back towards the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pass on' looks like handing something along, but here it is a polite way of saying to die.
explanation.definitionFit: Readier is the comparative of ready, so it means more fully prepared.

clue.text: It's no good to be upstanding

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to be is to live, to exist

explanation.surface: A remark that being honest and upright is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstanding' turns LIVE upward to give the answer in this down clue; the surface makes it sound like moral uprightness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wicked is the opposite of good, a bad thing.

clue.text: Went back over to see retired people ensconced

indicators.note: ensconced means settled snugly within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: RETD is the standard abbreviation for retired
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Someone returning to visit pensioners settled in their homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ensconced' puts RACE inside RETD, the abbreviation for retired; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrace steps is to go along the same route again.

clue.text: Hide from a monitor

definitions.meaning: to hide is to shield from view
a monitor is a display ... for a computer or television

explanation.surface: Concealing oneself away from a computer display.
explanation.definitionFit: Screening something conceals it, and a computer display panel is also called this.

clue.text: Be thankful for increase in value

definitions.meaning: to rise in worth, as property does

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both feeling grateful for something and an asset growing in worth over time.

clue.text: Miss Liddell bears church goblet

indicators.note: in a down clue, the lower piece bears or supports the one above it

parts.note: Alice Liddell was the girl who inspired Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A young woman carrying a cup used in a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'bears' means the girl's name sits underneath and holds up the church abbreviation. Alice Liddell was the real girl behind Lewis Carroll's Alice.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a large cup or goblet, especially the one holding communion wine.

clue.text: A star needs charisma

explanation.surface: A celebrity requires magnetic charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity is often called a TV figure of this kind, and strong character or charm is also meant.

clue.text: Cooling device for heating device

definitions.meaning: in a car engine this part dissipates heat to keep the engine cool
in a house this panel warms the room

explanation.surface: A cooler sold as something to warm you up.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a car engine's cooling unit and a household room heater.

clue.text: Expert fitness fanatic needs calm

parts.note: PE is physical education, school fitness lessons
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A skilled gym enthusiast wants tranquillity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert fitness fanatic' reads as a PE ace, someone brilliant at PE, so the pieces are PE then ACE; 'needs' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace is a state of quiet tranquillity, freedom from disturbance.

clue.text: Unruly child a bit crazy in the morning

parts.note: a little means a bit
mad means crazy
AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster going slightly mad before noon.
explanation.definitionFit: A little madam is a bossy, badly behaved girl in British usage.

clue.text: A master retired as result of bloomer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, standing for 'a'

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: sir is a title for a master

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster retiring because of a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reverses only the title for a master. 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An iris is a flowering plant, and a bloomer here means something that blooms.

clue.text: Reckless types challenged by things that are wrong

parts.note: dared means challenged someone to do something
evils are wrongs or wicked things

explanation.surface: Risk-takers provoked into misdeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Daredevils are people who take foolhardy risks for thrills.

clue.text: Irishman embraced by father of the house?

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside another piece

parts.note: a father is a parent
Liam is a typical Irish man's name

explanation.surface: An Irish MP hugged by the longest-serving member, the Father of the House.
explanation.walkthrough: The Father of the House is the title of the longest-serving MP in the UK House of Commons, so the surface sits in Westminster.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislative chamber is called a house, as in the House of Commons.

clue.text: Aren't the changes meant to intimidate

indicators.note: changes tells us the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether the alterations were meant to frighten people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' signals the anagram of AREN'T THE; 'meant to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace someone is to frighten them with warnings of harm.

clue.text: When trapped I have to yield

indicators.note: trapped means held inside another piece

parts.note: given, as in 'given that', can mean when

explanation.surface: A captive saying they must surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped' puts I inside GIVEN; 'have to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To give in is to surrender or concede.

clue.text: Panelling was put round stylish little dwelling

indicators.note: put round means the word goes around another piece

parts.note: in means fashionable
a cot is a small cottage

explanation.surface: Wooden boards fitted around a smart little cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put round' looks like a phrase about installing panels; it tells us the past tense of 'be' wraps around the word for stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot is wooden panelling lining the lower part of a room's walls.

clue.text: Aim to get everyone into finale

indicators.note: into here means following on into, so one piece comes after the other

parts.note: the end is the finale
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A plan to get the whole cast into the closing number.
explanation.walkthrough: The sense of aim comes from the phrase 'be-all and end-all'; 'into' means the second piece follows on from the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The end-all is the ultimate goal or purpose.

clue.text: Intimidating woman set about old soldier

indicators.note: set about means placed around another piece

parts.note: a dragon is a fierce, formidable woman

explanation.surface: A fearsome woman attacking a veteran trooper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' looks like 'attack' but puts DRAGON around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoon was a mounted infantryman, a type of cavalry trooper.

clue.text: Earlier ages said to be idyllic

parts.note: the past is earlier ages
oral means spoken, said

explanation.surface: Bygone times claimed to be perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral describes an idealised, peaceful country life.

clue.text: Managed to continue making capital

parts.note: ran means managed, as a business
go on means continue

explanation.surface: Someone succeeding in keeping going to amass funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but is a capital city, Rangoon being the former capital of Burma.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon, now Yangon, was formerly the capital city of Burma.

clue.text: Last transfer to a German camp

indicators.note: transfer suggests the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A final move to a camp in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transfer' makes STAL from LAST; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp.

clue.text: Maybe detain a man of unyielding nature

indicators.note: maybe suggests the words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A suggestion to hold someone who is stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals the anagram of DETAIN A MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamantine means extremely hard and unbreakable, like adamant.

clue.text: Make clothing with name incorporated

indicators.note: incorporated means taken into the body of another piece

parts.note: kit is a set of clothing

explanation.surface: Producing garments with a label sewn in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporated' puts N inside KIT; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to make by interlocking loops of yarn.

clue.text: He races in spectacles

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of spectacles
TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races

explanation.surface: A man who drives competitively wearing glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT races are motorcycle races on the Isle of Man; two Os look like a pair of glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a man's name, so it can stand for a male person.

clue.text: Home found for a fellow oriental

parts.note: bod is informal British for a person or fellow
E stands for eastern, oriental

explanation.surface: A house found for an Asian man.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a dwelling place.

clue.text: Spot financier covered in medical cream

indicators.note: covered in means placed inside another piece

parts.note: a lotion is a medical cream
CA is chartered accountant, a financial professional

explanation.surface: A banker smeared with ointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'financier' stands for a chartered accountant, abbreviated to two letters; 'covered in' says it sits inside the cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A location is a place or site.

clue.text: Where racing drivers are up against it

definitions.meaning: literally, cars taking a sharp bend on a track

explanation.surface: Motorsport competitors under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in difficulty, and literally describes cars negotiating a sharp bend.
